Detect transitions

detect_transition.Rd

Tracks how entities move between groups, such as paygrades or departments, over time. A move happens when an entity joins a group it did not hold in its previous period, and pairs each group it held then with each group it joins, returning one record per transition

Usage

detect_transition(data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
detect_transition(
  data,
  id_col = "personnel_id",
  group_col,
  drop_duplicates = FALSE,
  across_separations = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_dbi'
detect_transition(
  data,
  id_col = "personnel_id",
  group_col,
  drop_duplicates = FALSE,
  across_separations = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or remote database table (tbl_dbi) with a ref_date column, the identifier column and the grouping column.

...

Arguments passed to methods.

id_col

Character. Column identifying whose career is tracked, such as a person or a contract. Default "personnel_id".

group_col

Character. Column defining a group, such as a paygrade or a department. To track a combination of groups, such as paygrade within department, combine them into one column beforehand (e.g., paste(paygrade, department, sep = "|")).

drop_duplicates

Logical. Drop every entity with more than one record on the same ref_date, with a warning, so that each entity belongs to a single group per period. Default FALSE, which keeps entities belonging to several groups at once. See Details.

across_separations

Logical. Count moves made across a separation, i.e. between the groups an entity held before leaving the public sector and those it holds on its return. Default FALSE, which treats the return as the start of a new career. See Details.

Value

One row per move with the identifier, from (a group held in the period before the move), to (a group joined), from_date (when the entity began holding from without a break) and ref_date (when the entity was first seen in to). A data.table for data frame input; a lazy table for tbl_dbi input (use dplyr::collect() to bring it into memory).

Details

Each move is dated when it happens: ref_date is the first period the entity is seen in its new group. Dating it by when the entity entered its previous group would instead push every first move back to the start of the data.

An entity may belong to several groups on the same date, such as two occupations. Each group it held in its previous period is paired with each group it joins, so holding A and B and then A and C gives two moves, A -> C and B -> C. Leaving a group without joining another, such as holding A and B and then only A, is not a move. Several records in the same group, such as two contracts in the same paygrade, hold it once.

With drop_duplicates = TRUE, an entity with more than one record on a date, even in the same group, is dropped entirely, with a warning saying how many records were removed.

An entity may separate itself from the public sector and return later in time. By default its return starts a new career: the groups it held before leaving are the last of the old career, and the groups it returns to are not moves. Pass only the records in which entities are active, such as active contracts, so that inactive periods count as separations. With across_separations = TRUE, separations are ignored, so a move can span dates on which the entity is missing.

Rows with a missing identifier or group are silently dropped.

See also

compute_transition(), which counts these moves. plot_transition_network() to draw them as a network.

Examples

careers <- data.frame(
  personnel_id = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "b"),
  ref_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2022-01-01",
    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2021-01-01"
  )),
  paygrade = c("G1", "G1", "G2", "A", "B", "A", "C")
)
detect_transition(careers, group_col = "paygrade")
#>    personnel_id   from     to  from_date   ref_date
#>          <char> <char> <char>     <Date>     <Date>
#> 1:            a     G1     G2 2020-01-01 2022-01-01
#> 2:            b      A      C 2020-01-01 2021-01-01
#> 3:            b      B      C 2020-01-01 2021-01-01

# b holds two paygrades at once, so is dropped
detect_transition(careers, group_col = "paygrade", drop_duplicates = TRUE)
#> Warning: 2 record(s) are not uniquely identified by `personnel_id` and `ref_date`; dropping all 4 record(s) for the 1 affected `personnel_id` value(s).
#>    personnel_id   from     to  from_date   ref_date
#>          <char> <char> <char>     <Date>     <Date>
#> 1:            a     G1     G2 2020-01-01 2022-01-01

# c leaves after 2020 and returns to a different paygrade in 2022
returns <- data.frame(
  personnel_id = "c",
  ref_date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2022-01-01")),
  paygrade = c("G1", "G2")
)
detect_transition(rbind(careers, returns), group_col = "paygrade")
#>    personnel_id   from     to  from_date   ref_date
#>          <char> <char> <char>     <Date>     <Date>
#> 1:            a     G1     G2 2020-01-01 2022-01-01
#> 2:            b      A      C 2020-01-01 2021-01-01
#> 3:            b      B      C 2020-01-01 2021-01-01
detect_transition(
  rbind(careers, returns),
  group_col = "paygrade",
  across_separations = TRUE
)
#>    personnel_id   from     to  from_date   ref_date
#>          <char> <char> <char>     <Date>     <Date>
#> 1:            a     G1     G2 2020-01-01 2022-01-01
#> 2:            b      A      C 2020-01-01 2021-01-01
#> 3:            b      B      C 2020-01-01 2021-01-01
#> 4:            c     G1     G2 2020-01-01 2022-01-01
